content_metadata.description: An interview discussing ARM's newly launched Cortex-M processors, focusing on security features, ARMv8-M architecture, and the future of IoT.

qAndA.answer: The new processors include TrustZone, the TrustZone Security Foundation, secure key storage, and a new cryptography product.
qAndA.question: What specific security features are included in the new processors?

qAndA.answer: The ARMv8-M architecture offers two profiles - baseline and mainline - allowing for easier migration between different Cortex-M cores.
qAndA.question: What is the advantage of the ARMv8-M architecture for scalability?

qAndA.answer: The Cortex-M33 maintains the same energy efficiency as the Cortex-M4, while the Cortex-M23 matches the energy efficiency of the Cortex-M0+.
qAndA.question: How does ARM ensure energy efficiency with the new processors?

qAndA.answer: It shows the industry acceptance and anticipation for the new processors and highlights the collaborative effort in building a secure IoT ecosystem.
qAndA.question: What is the significance of the seven lead partners announced for the new processors?

qAndA.answer: The interview starts with a neutral, curious mood and shifts towards excitement as industry adoption and the anticipation for future releases are discussed.
qAndA.question: What is the overall mood of the interview?

timecoded_text_to_speech.text: The Arm Techcon 2016, and who are you?
I'm Tom
This is a big deal, right? This is the first time you have an Arm V8M.
Correct, so these are two new processors on the new architecture, the ARM V8M architecture.
And these are the first processors which include Trouson, the very first small KotExM, including Trouson.
We have the KotExM23 which is optimized for the smallest areas, smallest power, for the most constrained IoT nodes.
We have the KotExM33 which is offering much more features, better so on the V8M architecture, having Trouson, but also new features like the cross-saintor face, it has DSP, it has the SPU.
So yeah, definitely for more capable IoT nodes.
So is the upgrade for KotExM0 plus and KotExM4, KotExM3?
I'm not sure if the upgrade is the right word, it's complementary to the existing products.
So the M0 plus, M0, M3, M4, M7 will remain, and this is now bringing more security, so the Trouson security foundation,
that's at the very heart of these processors, and we believe our processor will still coexist.
But yes, if you are building a security IoT nodes, you'd be disserved with the M23 or the KotExM3.
So what's the main advantage of the KotEx, the Rm V8M, and what is security, is a lot about security?

Correct, so there's security, with Trouson and with other features, there's also a much better scalability, so within the architecture of the M, we have two profiles, we have the baseline profile, on which is BayZ KotExM23,
and we have the mainline profile, which is the basis of the KotExM33, and it's very smooth now to move from the baseline to the main architecture,

it's about system level, in terms of number of interrupt, in terms of instructions, and it makes both for the two designers and for the processor developer, which is more easy to migrate from one core to the other.
And so it's very, very important, it's the biggest, most important thing right now for IoT, is security, right?
Correct, you're solving this right now?
Yes, so we are solving, in fact, many things, there is security, the Trouson security for foundation, we are still also very power aware,
so even with security, the KotExM33, we have the same energy efficiency as the KotExM4, and the KotExM23, will remain the same energy efficiency within M0+.
So for IoT, yes, security is key, but also cost and energy efficiency.
Does it go in lower nanometer?
Yes.
Is that part of the considerations right here to save power consumption?
Yes, it will, but you know all our processors are, in fact, processed agnostic, so you can build, because M23 or M43, on any kind of process.
Okay, so all the process are like 180 nanometers, down to 40 nanometers, 28, 16, 10, whatever you need, in fact.
So as your job, talking with all the customers and the do KotExM, and talking to them and saying, hey, it's great idea, you should use the M33 or the 23 and...
So in fact, my job indeed is to be the interface between the customers, the problems they have to solve and our engineering.
In fact, we don't really have to sell your product now, because if you look at the announcement, we have already seven official lead partners.
We have a drug device, we have silicon labs, we have ST, we've got microchip, we have a new button, for example.
So in fact, the products are already well accepted, so the M23 and M43 are already in design at our partners, and we expect to have the first chip from our lead partners somewhere next year.
And MbedoS, MbedCloud, all that security stuff is going to be ready for this?
Yes, correct. So it's part of the bigger picture. So we're launching processors, we're also launching a system IP for security.
So they are the coding system IP, SSE 200, SIE 200.
We're also launching a new crypto-cell product for Twinense and to fortify the system.
With cryptography, with secure key storage, we're also launching radio, with the core radio, and all the MbedoS supporting BPM, and also the MbedCloud.
So it's very easy, the complete chain of security from the node, from the sensor, up to the server.
All right, so looking forward to a secure IoT embedded world.
With our partners and with the ecosystem, definitely yes.
Thank you very much.

youtube_description: Thomas Ensergueix is the ARM Cortex-M Product Manager, talks about the launch of ARM Cortex-M33 and ARM Cortex-M23, based on the latest ARMv8-M architecture with ARM TrustZone security and digital signal processing. You can read more at https://www.arm.com/products/processors/cortex-m/cortex-m33-processor.php and https://www.arm.com/products/processors/cortex-m/cortex-m23-processor.php
